config.primary_outcome: Validation accuracy after the final (third) fine-tuning epoch; no epoch or checkpoint selection. Per-epoch values and the odd calibration half are secondary.
primary_comparisons: After fine-tuning, is multi_q still better than random, paired_pruned and quaternion_exact at the same budget (paired by training seed)?
Does the multi_q - multi_full_projected difference survive fine-tuning?
Real control: multi_real vs random/pair_merge after fine-tuning
Matched savings (CNN6): quaternion vs real drop from each family's fine-tuned baseline
config.scope: Same compact models as results/multisource_compensation (rebuilt deterministically and checked against its frozen maps). The uncompressed baseline gets the same fine-tuning budget as a control for extra training. Every policy of one training seed sees identical batch order and augmentations. Only the first three random victim sets are fine-tuned (compute budget), for both random and multi_*_random. Fixed hyperparameters chosen a priori (10x below the original peak LR); none are tuned on validation. Quaternion consumers remain QuaternionConv2d during fine-tuning, so the Hamilton structure is kept.
